tldr: Sierra, co-founded by former Salesforce CEO Bret Taylor, is raising $1.75B at a $30B valuation — roughly doubling in under a year. The company has over $400M ARR from enterprise AI customer-service agents priced on outcomes, not seats.
context:
Sierra raised $950M at a $15B valuation in May 2026, led by Greenoaks. Less than seven months later, it's reportedly raising $1.75B at $30B — a valuation that puts it among the most valuable private AI companies.

The company builds AI agents that handle enterprise customer service. Its differentiator is outcome-based pricing: customers pay for resolved issues rather than per-seat licences. This aligns Sierra's incentives with its customers' in a way traditional SaaS pricing doesn't.

At $400M+ ARR, Sierra's $30B valuation implies a 75× revenue multiple. For comparison, Salesforce trades at roughly 8× revenue. The gap reflects the market's belief that AI-native customer service will grow much faster than traditional CRM.

Bret Taylor co-founded Sierra after serving as Salesforce CEO and co-CEO, and before that as CTO. His enterprise relationships and credibility are a significant part of the company's moat.
whyPM:
Sierra's outcome-based pricing is the most interesting signal for product leaders. When a vendor charges per resolved issue instead of per seat, it forces transparency about what 'resolution' means — and it makes the vendor accountable for quality in a way seat-based pricing never does.

The $30B valuation at 75× revenue also says something about where investors think enterprise AI is headed: toward agents that own entire workflows, not tools that assist humans. If Sierra can sustain $400M+ ARR on this model, it validates the thesis that AI agents can replace, not just augment, customer-service teams.

For product leaders in customer-facing businesses: the question isn't whether to use AI for customer service. It's whether to build your own agents, buy from Sierra, or risk being disrupted by a competitor who does either.
bull: Sierra's outcome pricing becomes the standard for enterprise AI. The company reaches $1B ARR by 2028 and IPOs at $50B+. Every customer-service SaaS vendor is forced to match the model or lose share.
bear: 75× revenue is a bubble multiple. Enterprise sales cycles slow as buyers test whether AI agents actually resolve issues or just deflect them. Sierra's ARR growth decelerates and the next round is flat or down.
unknowns: Whether the round has closed or is still in negotiations
